issues.description: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None, letting the literal string 'None' flow into the constructed koji URL.
issues.detail: When the regex fails to match, the function returns None and the caller interpolates it directly into the f-string, producing '/latest/None/Packages/...'. This is silent data corruption that surfaces later as a 404 far from the cause. Either raise on miss or have the caller handle the None case explicitly.

issues.description: Arch is read from the whole URL via regex instead of from the canonical NEVRA filename suffix.
issues.detail: Every RPM filename ends in .<arch>.rpm — the authoritative source. Regex-scanning the full URL creates a second source of truth that can disagree (e.g. an arch token appearing elsewhere in the path mis-classifies). noarch is also a legal arch and is unhandled. Read arch from the NEVRA filename suffix and include noarch in the recognized set.

issues.description: nevra[0] grabs the filename's first character, not the package name's first letter, obscuring the koji Packages-directory convention.
issues.detail: The koji Packages tree is keyed by the lowercased first letter of the package name. The code uses nevra[0] on the full filename, which coincides today but reads as accidental. Rename the variable to filename and compute first_letter from a properly-parsed package name so the invariant is explicit and robust.

issues.description: The koji path layout is leaked through inline string concatenation instead of a named helper or data.
issues.detail: The '/latest/{arch}/Packages/{first-letter}/{nevra}' shape is an external Fedora koji contract, not a fact about this function. Inlining it as splits and concatenation scatters the layout. Extract a build_koji_url(nevra, arch) helper or module-level layout data so future koji changes are a one-line edit and the structure is inspectable.

issues.description: Race condition between bump-lockfile commit and coreos-koji-tagger is acknowledged in the PR but undocumented in code.
issues.detail: The constructed URL is only valid after coreos-koji-tagger processes the merge commit — a temporal precondition that lives only in the PR description. A module-level docstring or comment naming this assumption would protect future maintainers from reusing the function in a context where the precondition does not hold.

issues.description: Regex with word boundaries is overkill for a fixed four-arch list inside a slash-delimited URL.
issues.detail: The data is a slash-delimited path; a simple split('/') and set-intersection against a module-level ARCHES tuple would be self-evident and let the arch list be reused elsewhere in the file. The compiled regex reads as cleverness for n=4. Let the data shape drive the algorithm.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a reasonable workaround for a DNF5 baseurl bug but the URL-rewriter has tight contract and data-modeling problems that should be fixed before merge. Two concrete correctness hazards dominate: a None return from extract_arch_from_url silently produces URLs containing the literal 'None', and arch is read from the whole URL via regex rather than from the canonical NEVRA filename suffix (which also leaves noarch unhandled). nevra[0] indexing the filename rather than the package name works only by accident. Beyond that, the koji path layout should live behind a single helper, and the race condition with coreos-koji-tagger deserves an in-code comment. Shape is right; tighten the boundary.
